$comment: Pipeline config for tools/boundaries/{snapshot,build}.py. Each entry under 'inputs' is one logical boundary layer the build runs today; entries under 'staged_inputs' are catalogued gap-fills (per docs/reference/boundary-data-sources.md §'gap-fill, not bulk-swap') that are NOT yet built — build.py and snapshot.py iterate 'inputs' only, so staged entries are inert until promoted. The `source` block separates *where the bytes come from* (urls, format) from *what we publish* (a GeoJSON at datasets/boundaries/in/geojson/<id>.geojson plus a sidecar). Adding a new upstream format (shapefile zip, geojsonl_7z, GeoPackage, GeoParquet) is an additive change to source.format, not a rewrite of the scripts. See tools/boundaries/README.md for the rationale.

inputs.id_property_note: Confirmed via Phase D.0 snapshot 2026-05-26. State_LGD is the LGD numeric state code (integer; joins via taxonomy.entities.lgd_code which is a zero-padded string — MapChoropleth's `to-number` coercion bridges the two via the JOIN_KEYS dispatch in frontend/src/lib/boundaries.ts). STNAME is the canonical state name (uppercase). Note the property casing differs from the districts entry (state_lgd / stname snake_case) — LGD_States publishes State_LGD / STNAME / STCODE11 / STNAME_SH / Remarks / OBJECTID / Shape_Length / Shape_Area / InPoly_FID / SimPgnFlag / MaxSimpTol / MinSimpTol verbatim from BharatMaps and we keep that shape intact.
inputs.coord_precision_note: coord_precision=2 (~1.1 km). Matches the districts entry; Douglas-Peucker simplification at 0.010° (per LAYER_TUNING['state'] in tools/boundaries/simplify.py) brings raw geometry under the 200 KB gzipped ceiling asserted by boundaries-conform.test.ts.

inputs.$comment: GAP-FILL (active): India district polygons keyed by LGD code. Sourced from ramSeraph's LGD_Districts release (BharatMaps/LGD lineage), shipped as 7z-compressed GeoJSONL. snapshot.py handles source.format='geojsonl_7z' (py7zr extraction, NDJSON->FeatureCollection wrap). Frontend join target: district.lgd_code field per ADR-0015. Source catalogue + per-component verdict: docs/reference/lgd-opendata.md and docs/reference/boundary-data-sources.md.
inputs.license_note: CC0 1.0 with requested attribution to datameet and the original government publisher (LGD/Bharatmaps). Underlying upstream service: https://mapservice.gov.in/gismapservice/rest/services/BharatMapService/Admin_Boundary_Village/MapServer/1
inputs.id_property_note: Confirmed via first snapshot 2026-05-13. dist_lgd is the LGD numeric district code (joins to district.lgd_code per ADR-0015); dtname is the canonical district name. Upstream also ships stname/state_lgd (state context), stcode11/dtcode11 (Census 2011), and topology cruft (OBJECTID, SHAPE_Length, SHAPE_Area, etc.) kept verbatim — inert for our consumers.
inputs.coord_precision_note: coord_precision=2 (~1.1 km). At precision=3 the file is 39 MB (over the 12 MB SNAPSHOT_BYTE_BUDGET); at 2 it lands ~6.5 MB. 1.1 km is well below typical district width (10-50 km) so choropleth rendering at zoom 3-9 is visually unaffected.

inputs.$comment: GAP-FILL: Survey-of-India national silhouette (single polygon, no admin codes). Used as the canonical India outline at country zoom in lieu of GADM-style derivatives; matches ECI/MoSPI cartographic convention. Separate license blanket from the ramSeraph layers below — yashveeeeeeer/india-geodata states CC-BY-4.0 derivative of SoI under National Geospatial Policy 2022 (Fowler v4 nit 3, TODO/TN-GRANULAR-GEO-PLAN.md Phase 1b). Incidental fix shipped with D.7 PR #431 (2026-05-27): vintage was empty string here, but boundary_layers_seed.py was bumped to 'operator-snapshot-2026-05' in PR #272 without re-syncing this entry — leaving boundary_layers.parquet's country row with a stale source_id that compile_to_parquet (--preserve-existing path) rejected on every subsequent partial snapshot. ADR-0042 operator-snapshot anchor.
inputs.license_note: yashveeeeeeer/india-geodata states CC-BY-4.0; the underlying SoI master is governed by India's National Geospatial Policy 2022. Separate license blanket from the ramSeraph mirrors used for LGD-keyed administrative layers.

inputs.$comment: Lok Sabha Parliamentary Constituency boundaries for the 2024 General Election (543 numbered + 2 J&K-territory placeholders with ls_seat_code=999 = 545 features total). Boundary decisions issued by Election Commission of India (Press Note No. 23, https://elections24.eci.gov.in/docs/press-note-no-23.pdf); geometry digitised by shijithpk from the press-note PDF images via QGIS and republished at github.com/shijithpk/2024_maps_supplement under The Unlicense. Researcher-quality, NOT survey-grade -- upstream README warns 'international borders will be off, use at your own risk' so this layer is suitable for choropleth visualisation but NOT for area/distance calculation. Underlying Delimitation Commission Orders: 1976 baseline + 2008 amendment + 2022 J&K Delimitation Commission Order + 2023 Assam Delimitation Commission Order. The 2 ls_seat_code=999 features cover J&K territory claimed by India but administered by Pakistan/China -- frontend MUST render them with a distinct treatment (e.g. diagonal hatch) and never tint them with election colours; this is a cartography contract, not just a rendering preference. Delivered as a local file under datasets/ephemeral/ rather than fetched live because the upstream repo has no permalinked release artifact for the consolidated 545-feature collection (only per-state shapefiles + reconstruction scripts). The local path is the snapshot we accept; replacing it requires deliberate operator action.

source_triple.title: India Lok Sabha Parliamentary Constituency boundaries (georeferenced)

inputs.id_property_note: ECI assigns each PC a numeric pc_no scoped within st_name (e.g. Tamil Nadu PC 1..39, Karnataka PC 1..28). The 2 features at ls_seat_code=999 carry st_name='Jammu and Kashmir' (Indian territory administered by Pakistan/China). Joining election results to geometry requires the (st_name, pc_no) tuple, not pc_no alone.

staged_inputs.$comment: TIEBREAKER (Assam): post-2023-delim AC layer from BharatMaps/LGD.
